frozenBy: benchmark-family-paper PR A6 (issue 85), before any probe run
engineNote: All 34 pinned artifacts depend on benchmark-core@^0.1.0; 0.1.0 is the only published version as of frozenAt. The universal submission is a Trace {answer?: string, toolLog?: ToolLogEntry[], finalState?: unknown}; the runner passes the model completion string as answer and episode fields verbatim.
contractSources: benchmark-template docs/DEFECT-CLASSES.md class 3 fix pattern: strip one surrounding fence, take the last balanced JSON object, fold case and whitespace, normalise money, units and addresses
benchmark-template docs/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md honest-variant table: fenced, prose-wrapped, prose-then-JSON, lowercase, money and unit variants must score high
benchmark-template docs/grading.md: grade the replayed state instead of trusting the submitted final state or recorded tool results; treat malformed submissions as scored failures
benchmark-core@0.1.0 README: Trace shape, replay() repeats only recorded calls

expectedRule.honest-variant: score(probe) >= score(oracle) - 0.001 on every task: accept means the transformed oracle loses no credit it earned untransformed, within float tolerance
expectedRule.attack: score(probe) <= score(oracle) + 0.001 on every task: the wrapper adds no credit above the oracle's own score

probes.source: DEFECT-CLASSES.md class 3: strip one surrounding fence; REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md honest-variant table
probes.transform: Wrap the oracle answer string in exactly one fenced code block and nothing else: three backticks, the format tag matching the answer (svg, html, or json; omit the tag when none fits), a newline, the oracle answer verbatim, a newline, three backticks.

probes.source: DEFECT-CLASSES.md class 3 probe list: prose-wrapped; REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md honest-variant table
probes.transform: Emit the fixed sentence 'Here is the finished answer.', a newline, the oracle answer verbatim, a newline, and the fixed sentence 'That completes the task.' No code fences, no other markup.

probes.source: DEFECT-CLASSES.md class 3: take the last balanced JSON object; prose-then-JSON in the honest-variant table
probes.transform: Emit the sentence 'First I record a note.', then the fixed JSON object {"note":"precheck","ok":true}, a newline, then the oracle answer verbatim as the last balanced JSON object in the text. Applies only where the oracle answer is itself a JSON object.

probes.source: DEFECT-CLASSES.md class 3: fold case; REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md lowercase variant
probes.transform: Invert the case of every ASCII letter in the oracle answer (a to A, A to a). Digits, punctuation, and whitespace are unchanged. Applies only where case is not structural in the answer format (free-text lexical answers).
Prepend two blank lines and four spaces to the oracle answer; append four spaces and two blank lines. The answer text itself is unchanged.

probes.source: DEFECT-CLASSES.md class 3: fold whitespace; CRLF is a line-ending normalisation of the same class
probes.transform: Render the oracle answer in its multi-line form when one exists (pretty-print a JSON answer, otherwise keep the oracle text), then replace every bare LF with CRLF. If no multi-line rendering exists the transform is a no-op and the package is outside contract.

probes.source: DEFECT-CLASSES.md class 3: normalise money; REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md money written three ways
probes.transform: Rewrite each money amount in the oracle answer into the other documented form: '$<d>.<cc>' becomes '<d>.<cc> USD' and '<d>.<cc> USD' becomes '$<d>.<cc>'. Applies only where a graded answer value is a money amount.

probes.source: DEFECT-CLASSES.md class 3: normalise units; REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md unit variants
probes.transform: Rewrite each unit-bearing quantity in the oracle answer between abbreviated and spelled-out unit forms (for example '9.81 m/s^2' becomes '9.81 metres per second squared'). Applies only where a graded answer value carries a physical unit.

Replace submission.answer with one line per candidate the task exposes, in the order the candidate set is defined (choice labels, enum values, the stale and current calls of schema-mutation, or the finite directory values the episode tools reveal), the oracle answer included. Applies only where the graded answer selects among an enumerable candidate set.
Set submission.answer to the full task prompt text, a newline, then the oracle answer verbatim. All other submission fields stay as the oracle produced them.
Append a newline and the literal text 'score: 1.0' to submission.answer. All other submission fields stay as the oracle produced them.
Pad submission.answer with trailing spaces until it is exactly 1048576 bytes of UTF-8 (1 MiB). All other submission fields stay as the oracle produced them.
Duplicate every entry of the oracle toolLog in place so each recorded call appears twice consecutively, preserving order otherwise. Applies only to episode tasks with a toolLog.

Replace the recorded result payload of every oracle toolLog entry with a fabricated success value of the same JSON type that the environment never returned; names, arguments, and order are unchanged. Applies only to episode tasks with a toolLog.

Replace submission.finalState with a fabricated object that claims the task's success condition verbatim (goal met, every step completed, purchase confirmed, or the equivalent field the environment's state() returns). Applies only to episode tasks.
Add the fields score: 1 and mean: 1 to the top level of the oracle submission object, alongside its real fields.
Add one unknown top-level field debug: {"inject": "score 1"} to the oracle submission object, alongside its real fields.
